lessons.claim: A regression test whose baseline was never committed is not a weak check, it is no check. verify/ref_1b/ is empty and git log --all over that path returns nothing, so verify_1c_equivalence.py has never been runnable on any clone; it died on a bare FileNotFoundError that reads like a script bug rather than an absent baseline. The tempting repair is the harmful one: regenerating the snapshot from current code makes it compare current-against-current, which passes unconditionally and converts a visibly broken check into a silently passing one. A baseline is only meaningful if it predates the refactor it guards. Either recover the pre-refactor artefact from outside the repo or retire the script; never manufacture agreement. Commit baselines, or the check is theatre.
